# Beyond Earth
## Interactive Exploration of the Solar System

### Created with R + Plotly

**Date:** `r format(Sys.Date(), "%B %d, %Y")`

---

## Why This Matters

Space exploration is no longer science fiction.  

With interactive visualizations we can:

- Compare planetary characteristics in real time  
- Understand scale and relationships  
- Spark curiosity about our cosmic neighborhood  

This presentation uses **Plotly** to make data exploration feel like a mission control dashboard.

---

## The Dataset

We will explore key properties of the planets in our Solar System:

| Planet     | Distance from Sun (AU) | Radius (Earth = 1) | Mass (Earth = 1) | Moons | Type      |
|------------|------------------------|--------------------|------------------|-------|-----------|
| Mercury    | 0.39                   | 0.38               | 0.055            | 0     | Terrestrial |
| Venus      | 0.72                   | 0.95               | 0.815            | 0     | Terrestrial |
| Earth      | 1.00                   | 1.00               | 1.000            | 1     | Terrestrial |
| Mars       | 1.52                   | 0.53               | 0.107            | 2     | Terrestrial |
| Jupiter    | 5.20                   | 11.21              | 317.8            | 95    | Gas Giant |
| Saturn     | 9.58                   | 9.45               | 95.2             | 146   | Gas Giant |
| Uranus     | 19.22                  | 4.01               | 14.5             | 28    | Ice Giant |
| Neptune    | 30.05                  | 3.88               | 17.1             | 16    | Ice Giant |

---

## Interactive Solar System Explorer

Hover over any point to see detailed information.  
You can zoom, pan, and explore relationships between distance, size, and mass.

```{r plotly-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
planets <- data.frame(
  Planet = c("Mercury", "Venus", "Earth", "Mars", "Jupiter", "Saturn", "Uranus", "Neptune"),
  Distance_AU = c(0.39, 0.72, 1.00, 1.52, 5.20, 9.58, 19.22, 30.05),
  Radius_Earth = c(0.38, 0.95, 1.00, 0.53, 11.21, 9.45, 4.01, 3.88),
  Mass_Earth = c(0.055, 0.815, 1.000, 0.107, 317.8, 95.2, 14.5, 17.1),
  Moons = c(0, 0, 1, 2, 95, 146, 28, 16),
  Type = c("Terrestrial", "Terrestrial", "Terrestrial", "Terrestrial",
           "Gas Giant", "Gas Giant", "Ice Giant", "Ice Giant"),
  Color = c("#A9A9A9", "#E6C35C", "#4A90D9", "#E27B58",
            "#E8A87C", "#F4D35E", "#7EC8E3", "#4169E1")
)

p <- plot_ly(
  data = planets,
  x = ~Distance_AU,
  y = ~Radius_Earth,
  size = ~Mass_Earth,
  color = ~Type,
  colors = c("Terrestrial" = "#4A90D9", "Gas Giant" = "#E8A87C", "Ice Giant" = "#7EC8E3"),
  text = ~paste0(
    "<b>", Planet, "</b><br>",
    "Distance: ", Distance_AU, " AU<br>",
    "Radius: ", Radius_Earth, " × Earth<br>",
    "Mass: ", Mass_Earth, " × Earth<br>",
    "Moons: ", Moons
  ),
  hoverinfo = "text",
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  marker = list(
    sizemode = "diameter",
    opacity = 0.85,
    line = list(width = 1, color = "#333")
  )
) %>%
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = "Solar System: Distance vs Size (bubble size = Mass)",
      font = list(size = 18, color = "#1a1a2e")
    ),
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Distance from Sun (Astronomical Units)",
      gridcolor = "#e0e0e0",
      zeroline = FALSE
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Radius (Earth = 1)",
      gridcolor = "#e0e0e0",
      zeroline = FALSE
    ),
    paper_bgcolor = "#f8f9fa",
    plot_bgcolor = "#ffffff",
    legend = list(
      title = list(text = "Planet Type"),
      bgcolor = "rgba(255,255,255,0.8)"
    ),
    hovermode = "closest",
    margin = list(l = 60, r = 40, t = 60, b = 60)
  ) %>%
  config(displayModeBar = TRUE, displaylogo = FALSE)

p
```

---

## Key Insights from the Interactive Plot

- **Terrestrial planets** (blue) cluster close to the Sun and are relatively small.  
- **Gas giants** (orange) dominate in both size and mass — Jupiter is a true heavyweight.  
- **Ice giants** (cyan) sit far out, with moderate size but still impressive mass.  
- Bubble size clearly shows that mass does not scale linearly with radius (density differences matter!).

Try hovering and zooming — the interactivity reveals patterns that static charts hide.

---

## Bonus: Mass vs Number of Moons

Another perspective on the data:

```{r plotly-plot2, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
p2 <- plot_ly(
  data = planets,
  x = ~Mass_Earth,
  y = ~Moons,
  color = ~Type,
  colors = c("Terrestrial" = "#4A90D9", "Gas Giant" = "#E8A87C", "Ice Giant" = "#7EC8E3"),
  text = ~paste0("<b>", Planet, "</b><br>Mass: ", Mass_Earth, " × Earth<br>Moons: ", Moons),
  hoverinfo = "text",
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers+text",
  textposition = "top center",
  marker = list(size = 16, opacity = 0.9)
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Planetary Mass vs Number of Known Moons",
    xaxis = list(title = "Mass (Earth = 1)", type = "log"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Number of Moons"),
    paper_bgcolor = "#f8f9fa",
    plot_bgcolor = "#ffffff"
  )

p2
```
